Independently re-ran verification script (all asserts pass) and recomputed Euclidean distances: vertex norms 2.0 and 1.9672 satisfy outer ball; min half-side 0.9 satisfies inner ball; 8 facets; centrally symmetric so centroid 0. Cone-volume per facet 2*prod(a), total 16*prod(a), normalized weight exactly 1/8 for every facet of any centered box, so V_P=V_Q=(1/8)sum_{+-e_i} and W_2=0 via identity coupling. Optimal-translation Hausdorff distance is exactly 0.2: x1-projection is 1-Lipschitz giving lower bound 0.2+|t1| for any translation t, and at t=0 Euclidean sup_Q=0.2, sup_P=sqrt(0.03)~0.173, so max is 0.2. Hence 0.2<=0 is false, disproving the fragment with any finite constant/exponent. Minor presentation note (script uses L_inf distance giving sup_P=0.1) does not change the Euclidean conclusion.

Hypotheses concern unnormalized measures and decomposition families, not the named 4D boxes, the uniform 1/8 normalized weights, W_2=0, or constants 20, 1/4, 1e-3.

material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Proves that for a single parallelotope each cone carries 1/(2n) of the volume, hence uniform 1/8 normalized weights for axis-aligned boxes. This is the intra-body background formula only; it does not state that two distinct boxes P and Q share the same normalized 8-point measure with Hausdorff distance 0.2 to refute the Wasserstein modulus.

material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Characterizes planar equality as dilates or parallelograms with parallel sides using the cone-volume probability measure. This is the 2D analogue of box non-uniqueness, but it is in dimension 2, names no 4D pair, and asserts no Wasserstein stability bound with the submitted constants and threshold.

material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Proves the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture and discusses equality/uniqueness for bodies with symmetries under n independent hyperplanes, the same symmetry class as the submitted boxes. The conclusion concerns unnormalized cone-volume equality implying a decomposition structure, not a normalized-measure collision of bodies with different total volumes nor the target Wasserstein inequality.
